title: Indian stroke speech corpus / Characterizing stroke-affected speech using F0 and duration-based features
task: five sustained vowels (each twice); three-word phonetically rich read sentences
token_or_recording_size: 50 stroke + 50 healthy speakers; five sustained vowels x2 per participant plus sentence recordings
annotation_target: manually segmented sustained-vowel utterances and sentence utterances; F0 contour statistics; automatically derived transition/steady-state timing features
manual_scope: raw audio manually segmented into independent vowel-category utterances; sentence recordings similarly segmented; transition-region boundaries themselves are algorithmic and must not be represented as manual
decision_reason: Primary Telugu clinical/control production corpus with explicit manual segmentation of the relevant recorded vowel and sentence utterances and a public Zenodo deposit.
evidence_summary: Scientific Reports methods state that raw audio was manually segmented into independent utterances for each vowel category and similarly for sentences. Corpus comprises 50 stroke patients and 50 healthy controls, all Telugu L1 speakers. Authors report F0 mean/median/SD and transition/non-transition duration-derived features; transition regions are automatically detected and should retain that provenance. Data availability identifies Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.15675906 / record 15675907.
